title: curl merges about 50 bugfixes from Joshua Rogers' ZeroPath-assisted scans; maintainer calls the reports a new breed of analyzer output
summary: In Sept 2025 curl received hundreds of candidate issues found mainly with the ZeroPath AI analyzer by Joshua Rogers; maintainer Daniel Stenberg merged about 50 bugfixes from the first list.
account: The reports arrived from mid-September 2025. Stenberg writes that a security report received on 16 September accurately identified a possible stack-based buffer overflow in curl's Kerberos FTP code. It was not turned into a CVE only because the code could not be reached. The project then removed krb5-ftp support. The reporter, Joshua Rogers, then forwarded a large list of further potential issues found mostly with ZeroPath, an AI-powered code analyzer. That produced over two hundred possible problems despite curl's existing compilers, static analyzers and fuzzing. From the initial list about 50 separately identifiable bugfixes were merged. Second and third lists of 47 and 158 items followed. Stenberg told The Register that about 50 bugfixes based on Rogers' reports had been merged. Rogers' retrospective states that about 98% of the curl bugs reported and fixed were discovered by ZeroPath. It puts the running total of fixed bugs around 150.
purpose: AI-powered static analysis of source code to find vulnerabilities and bugs.
system: ZeroPath AI code analyzer (with other scanners tested by Rogers)
deployer: Joshua Rogers (independent security researcher); fixes merged by the curl project
taxonomy_note: Bugfixes rather than confirmed vulnerabilities are read as risk reduced.

ratings.reason: About 50 merged bugfixes from the first list, a potential overflow identified and unused code removed, per the curl maintainer.
curl is widely deployed, but no user-facing incident was averted. The merged fixes are described as mostly small mistakes.

ai_role.statement: The maintainer confirms the reports' quality and the merged fixes. He notes he does not know the exact split between tool and human. Rogers attributes ~98% of the fixed curl bugs to ZeroPath. Both the deployer and the confirming maintainer are independent of the vendor.

headline: curl merges about 50 bugfixes from ZeroPath-assisted scans
metric: about 50 separately identifiable bugfixes were merged

comparator.against: curl's existing compilers, static analyzers and fuzzers (scan-build, clang-tidy, CodeSonar, Coverity, CodeQL, OSS-Fuzz), whose findings were already all fixed
comparator.before: we always address and fix every warning and complaint they report
comparator.after: over two hundred new potential problems
comparator.quote: In the curl project we continuously run compilers with maximum pickiness enabled and we throw scan-build, clang-tidy, CodeSonar, Coverity, CodeQL and OSS-Fuzz at it and we always address and fix every warning and complaint they report so it was a little surprising that this tool now suddenly could produce over two hundred new potential problems.

later.note: Rogers' retrospective of 19 October 2025 put curl's count of fixed ZeroPath-detected bugs at around 150 and expected about 200 within a week.
later.quote: At the moment, the curl project has fixed around 150 of the bugs detected by ZeroPath, but I believe that by the end of next week, it will be around 200.
